mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a month is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such FEDFUNDS spikes, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightening reduces speculative buying in equities.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during UNRATE > 4.5% months, or UNRATE remains below 4.5% throughout the observation window.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% for two consecutive months, it predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals robust demand for capital goods.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption growth
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such consumption outpacing production periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% for three months indicates supply-side contraction, which is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >= 8% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for four consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as low rates encourage equity investment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS stays below 4% for four months in non-crisis regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS below 130,000 jobs coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak hiring signals weak consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 130,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such hiring declines.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS above 400,000 (millions of dollars) in retail sales signal strong demand, predicting a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during high-RSAFS months.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 210 for two consecutive months, it indicates persistent price pressures that drive a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via equity valuation compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 210 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such CPI spikes.
